findings.title: Night transactions carry significantly elevated fraud risk
findings.finding: Fraud rate between 00:00–06:59 is 0.444% vs 0.136% during the day — a 3.3x relative risk. Chi-square test confirms this is not noise (χ²=141, p=1.4e-32).
findings.recommendation: Apply step-up authentication (OTP/3-D Secure) to night-time transactions above the median amount.

findings.title: Fraudulent amounts follow a different distribution
findings.finding: Median fraud amount is €9.82 vs €22.00 for legitimate transactions (Mann-Whitney U, p=2.7e-05). Fraudsters often probe with small amounts before larger attempts, so low-value anomalies matter as much as high-value ones.
findings.recommendation: Do not filter alerts purely by amount; small-amount anomalies on new patterns deserve scoring weight.

findings.title: Fraud concentrates in identifiable peak hours
findings.finding: The three riskiest hours (with 95% Wilson confidence intervals) are: 02:00 (1.451% [1.096–1.918%]), 04:00 (1.044% [0.696–1.561%]), 03:00 (0.488% [0.305–0.779%]). Overall portfolio baseline is 0.167%.
findings.recommendation: Staff manual-review queues to match the hourly risk curve rather than uniform coverage.

findings.title: Cost-tuned decision threshold beats the 0.5 default
findings.finding: Sweeping thresholds against a cost model (missed fraud = full transaction amount, false decline = €30 friction) puts the optimal operating point at t=0.86, saving €4,489 on the test window vs the default 0.5 (recall 74.7%, precision 68.3%).
findings.recommendation: Deploy with threshold 0.86; re-tune whenever the friction-cost assumption or fraud mix changes.

findings.title: A small behavioural segment concentrates outsized fraud
findings.finding: K-means segment 2 holds only 32.5% of transactions but 67.9% of all fraud — 2.1x the baseline rate, €25,454 of fraud value (avg ticket €44.41, 13% at night).
findings.recommendation: Route this segment to a stricter scoring threshold or rules overlay; it is the cheapest place to buy recall.

findings.title: Model performance on the held-out test set
findings.finding: XGBoost with SMOTE achieves recall 78.9%, precision 24.6%, AUC-ROC 0.967 and average precision 0.746 on 20% held-out data. With a 0.17% fraud base rate, average precision is the honest headline metric — accuracy is uninformative.
findings.recommendation: Track precision/recall at the deployed threshold weekly; alert if recall drops more than 5 points.
